plan.focus: Temescal's five businesses are all growing on paper, but the story is whether that growth reaches the people who actually live and work on the block — or whether it's just the ledger getting fatter while the sidewalk stays the same.
plan.why: Every business on this slice is up — revenue, headcount, all of it. That's rare enough to be suspicious. When the numbers all point one direction, the real story is usually in what they don't measure: who's getting left out, what's getting priced out, which worker is doing the same job for the same pay while the owner's revenue climbs. The desk wants the block, the counter, the hiring board. That's where I'm going.
checks: Confirm Gridiron Analytics' growth is actually translating to new hires on the ground, not just reclassifying existing staff.
Check whether Calderon-Nishi's construction work is on new builds or retrofits — that changes who benefits.
Verify if Temescal Community Health Center's revenue growth is tied to patient volume or grant funding — different stories entirely.
Ask whether OakTown Social's baristas have seen their hours or wages move with the revenue uptick.
Look at whether Da Dough's growth is keeping pace with rent on Telegraph or if Melton is working more for the same money.

targets.question: When you run the numbers on this block, what do you see that the public reports don't capture?
targets.basis: Ariana Reyes is a data analyst at Gridiron Analytics, the fastest-growing business on the slice — she reads the numbers for a living and can speak to what growth actually looks like from inside.

targets.question: Is the health center's growth reaching the people who need it most, or is it just a bigger budget line?
targets.basis: Bobby Chen-Ramirez is the project director at Temescal Community Health Center — he knows whether the revenue uptick is translating to services or just administration.

targets.question: What are you seeing in the walls of this block — which buildings are getting real investment and which are just getting patched?
targets.basis: Jett Walker is a plumber at Calderon-Nishi — he's inside the physical infrastructure of Temescal and can speak to whether the construction growth is real or surface-level.

plan.interpretation: The ledger shows uniform growth across five businesses in one neighborhood — that's the kind of clean picture that usually means the data is measuring something narrow. Revenue and headcount are up, but those metrics don't tell you who's benefitting. The pattern I'm tracking is the gap between the numbers and the lived experience of the people on the block — the barista whose hours didn't change, the baker whose rent went up, the patient whose copay stayed the same. That gap is the story.
unverifiedLead: Ariana Reyes may have insight into whether Gridiron's growth is concentrated among senior staff or spread across the whole team.
Bobby Chen-Ramirez might be able to speak to whether the health center's budget growth is keeping pace with patient demand or just covering rising costs.
Jett Walker could have observations about which buildings on Telegraph are getting real renovation work versus just cosmetic fixes.
plan.closeQuestion: If every business on the block is growing, why does it still feel like the neighborhood is being pulled in two directions?
